newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain oil official sees petrochemical growth.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain oil official sees petrochemical growth.

text.p: A Bahraini oil official said on Monday the petrochemical industry in the Arab world was experiencing a considerable increase in business and forecast more growth amid a rise in demand.

"The near future will witness more growth in this industry, given the steady increase in demand for raw materials and consumer products as a result of increasing economic growth rates worldwide," Mohammed Saleh al-Shaikh Ali said.
Ali, an undersecretary of Bahrain's Oil and Industry Ministry, was speaking at an Arab petrochemical industry integration conference which opened in Bahrain on Monday.

He noted Arab states, led by oil-producing countries, began establishing petrochemical industries in the 1970s "motivated by the need to diversify their sources of income and to develop their economies".
"The pioneering countries in this field were Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Egypt, whose efforts covered the basic, intermediate and finished petrochemical industries," he said.
"Now the Arab states' petrochemical products account for around 10 percent of total global output," he added.
Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp is the biggest petrochemical producer in the Middle East. It accounts for around five percent of the world's output.
General Manager of the Bahrain-based Gulf Petrochemical Industries Company Mustafa al-Sayed said Arab investment in the petrochemical industry was still "very modest".

"Global investments in this industry total $250 billion with East Asian countries having the lion's share (of investment) of 55 percent while the Arab states have a share of less than 10 percent," he said but gave no further details.
